Standard Errors of the Predicted Random Effects

Source: R/se_ranef.R
se_ranef.Rd

The predicted random effects (BLUPs, conditional modes) of a mixed model with their standard errors and limits, and optionally the predicted value of each level (fixed part plus random effect).

Two standard errors are available:

type = "prediction"

(the default) the prediction error SE, \(\sqrt{Var(\hat u - u)}\), from the inverse of the mixed model equations (Henderson's \(C_{22}\); SAS PROC MIXED RANDOM / SOLUTION, "Std Err Pred"). It includes the uncertainty of the estimated fixed effects, which matters most for a term that contains a fixed factor (e.g. Block:Variety with Variety fixed).

type = "conditional"

the conditional SE, \(\sqrt{Var(u \mid y)}\) with the fixed effects treated as known: lme4's ranef(condVar = TRUE), the numbers of se_ranef() in predictmeans 1.x. It is smaller.

Both treat the variance parameters as known (the usual plug-in), except for glmmTMB: there "conditional" is ranef(condVar = TRUE) of glmmTMB, which is TMB's sdreport() and includes the uncertainty of the fixed effects and of the variance parameters (so it can exceed "prediction", which inverts the \((\beta, b)\) block of TMB's joint precision, variance parameters known). Correlated terms, nested and crossed terms, glmmTMB structures (us, cs, ar1, ...) and lme correlation and variance structures are all covered, as the SEs come from the joint covariance of all random effects. For GLMMs, all values are on the link scale.

With predict = TRUE, each level gets its predicted value: for a random term with no fixed factor in it (Block), the overall mean (the fixed factors averaged with equal weights, as predictmeans; covariates at their means) plus \(\hat u\); for a term that contains fixed factors (Block:Variety, Variety fixed), the predicted mean of that fixed level plus \(\hat u\). Its SE is from the joint covariance of \((\hat\beta, \hat u - u)\), \(L C L'\) with \(L = [k', e_i]\) ("prediction" always). Only intercept rows get a prediction (random slopes: NA). For GLMMs the response scale is added by the inverse link (SE by the delta method).

Usage

se_ranef(
  object,
  rand_term = NULL,
  type = c("prediction", "conditional"),
  predict = FALSE,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

# S3 method for class 'pm_ranef'
print(x, n = 10, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object

An lmer, glmer, glmmTMB (conditional model), lme or semireg fit.

rand_term

Optional name of one grouping factor, e.g. "Block" or "Variety:Block" (lme: the level name, e.g. "Variety" for ~ 1 | Block/Variety).

type

"prediction" (default) or "conditional" (1.x); see Description.

predict

Add the predicted value of each level (see Description)?

conf_level

Confidence level of the limits.

x

A pm_ranef result.

n

Rows printed per group.

digits

Digits printed.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class pm_ranef: group, level, term, estimate (the BLUP), std.error, conf.low, conf.high (normal limits \(\hat u \pm z\,SE\): for "prediction" a prediction interval of \(u\)); with predict = TRUE also prediction, prediction.std.error, prediction.conf.low, prediction.conf.high, and for GLMMs response, response.std.error, response.conf.low, response.conf.high. attr(, "settings") records type, conf_level, limits, model_class, scale and conditional (what the conditional SE is for this class). as.list() gives the 1.x result: one matrix of SEs (levels x terms) per group, or that matrix only when rand_term was given.

References

Henderson, C. R. (1975). Best linear unbiased estimation and prediction under a selection model. Biometrics, 31, 423-447.

See also

varcomp, residplot, advice

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

library(predictmeans)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety + (1|Block/Variety), data = Oats)
se_ranef(fm, "Block")
#> Predicted random effects (BLUPs), prediction error SE; 95% normal prediction intervals of u
#> 
#> Block (6 levels)
#>  level        term estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>     VI (Intercept)   -6.260     8.342  -22.611    10.091
#>      V (Intercept)  -10.583     8.342  -26.934     5.768
#>    III (Intercept)   -6.530     8.342  -22.881     9.821
#>     IV (Intercept)   -4.706     8.342  -21.057    11.645
#>     II (Intercept)    2.657     8.342  -13.694    19.008
#>      I (Intercept)   25.422     8.342    9.071    41.773
se_ranef(fm, "Block", type = "conditional")     # 1.x numbers
#> Predicted random effects (BLUPs), conditional SE; 95% normal intervals from the conditional SE
#> 
#> Block (6 levels)
#>  level        term estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>     VI (Intercept)   -6.260     6.373  -18.751     6.232
#>      V (Intercept)  -10.583     6.373  -23.075     1.909
#>    III (Intercept)   -6.530     6.373  -19.022     5.962
#>     IV (Intercept)   -4.706     6.373  -17.198     7.786
#>     II (Intercept)    2.657     6.373   -9.835    15.149
#>      I (Intercept)   25.422     6.373   12.930    37.913
se_ranef(fm, "Variety:Block", predict = TRUE)   # cell values
#> Predicted random effects (BLUPs), prediction error SE; 95% normal prediction intervals of u
